chunks: And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:
"The sleep of the fasting person is worship, his silence is glorification, his deed is accepted, and his supplication is answered."

key_terms.الصَّائِمِ: the fasting person; one observing sawm (fasting)
key_terms.تَسْبِيحٌ: glorification; declaring the transcendence of Allah
key_terms.دُعَاؤُهُ: his supplication; his du'a to Allah
key_terms.عَمَلُهُ: his deed; the acts performed by the fasting person
key_terms.عِبَادَةٌ: worship; an act of devotion to Allah
key_terms.نَوْمُ: sleep; here, the resting state of the fasting person counted as worship

ai.seo_question: What are the virtues and spiritual effects of fasting in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the spiritual excellence of the fasting person and the elevated state that accompanies sawm (fasting). It teaches that even ordinary states such as sleep and silence become acts of worship and glorification, while the fasting person's deeds and du'a are granted special acceptance.
